specification.problem: Learn the parameters theta=(J_j,h_j) of a 1D transverse-field Ising chain by Bayesian (sequential Monte Carlo) inference, where each experiment's likelihood is computed on a Lieb-Robinson light-cone patch of at most 8 qubits simulated exactly. Scoped to one tiny instance: an 8-qubit chain standing in for the device, with a patch of at most 8 qubits, one Bayesian update per experiment.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single-round likelihood circuit on a patch of at most 8 qubits (product state |+>^m, exact or Trotterized evolution, measure one qubit in Z or X), plus the classical particle-filter update, resampling or Liu-West step, and an expected-information-gain experiment choice. Out of scope: the 50-qubit device, the actual epistemic velocity formula, interactive quantum learning details, pulse-level control optimization, the Fisher information bounds, and the 750 kb data figure.

symbols.meaning: number of qubits in the chain (patch size m<=8)
Lieb-Robinson velocity, depending on posterior uncertainty sigma

equations.label: Ising Hamiltonian
equations.latex: H(\theta)=\sum_j J_j Z_j Z_{j+1}+\sum_j h_j X_j
equations.description: 1D Ising model with unknown couplings and fields
equations.justification: Abstract names an Ising model simulator; the exact form is taken from the task sketch.

equations.label: Light-cone restriction
equations.description: Qubits within radius r of the measured qubit are simulated; v depends on the posterior spread, so it is epistemic
equations.abstract_quote: the Lieb–Robinson velocity is epistemic for our protocol, meaning that information propagates at a rate that depends on the uncertainty in the system Hamiltonian
equations.justification: The abstract says the velocity depends on the uncertainty. The functional form v(sigma) and the margin are not given.
assumptions: v(sigma) is a monotone function of posterior spread, unspecified

equations.label: Likelihood
equations.description: Born-rule outcome probability on the patch, computed per particle by statevector simulation
equations.justification: Standard quantum measurement; the patch approximates the full chain within the Lieb-Robinson tolerance.
assumptions: truncation error is controlled by the margin

equations.label: Bayes update
equations.description: Sequential Monte Carlo reweighting after each experiment
equations.abstract_quote: using Bayesian inference in concert with Lieb-Robinson bounds
equations.justification: Bayesian inference is stated; the particle-filter form is an assumed implementation.

equations.label: Liu-West resampling
equations.description: Resample particles and apply a kernel shift to preserve the posterior mean and covariance
equations.justification: Common SMC practice, used when the effective sample size is low.
assumptions: triggered when the effective sample size falls below a threshold

equations.label: Expected information gain
equations.description: Adaptive experiment design by maximizing mutual information between the outcome and theta
equations.justification: The sketch proposes maximizing information gain; the abstract only mentions interactive learning, so this is an assumed criterion.
assumptions: candidate set of finitely many (t,q,B) with t not small

registers.name: patch
registers.role: qubits of the light-cone patch simulated, initialized to |+>

specification.initial_state: |+>^{\otimes m} on the patch, prepared by H gates on |0>^m

steps.description: Initialize particles theta_k from a prior with weights 1/N.
Choose an experiment (t,q,B), e.g. by expected information gain.
Compute the light-cone radius from the current posterior spread and extract the patch.

For each particle, build the circuit: H on all patch qubits, then exact or Trotter evolution (RZZ with angle 2J_j dt, RX with angle 2h_j dt), then basis rotation and measurement or exact probability, giving the likelihood.
Take the device outcome d and update the weights, resampling with Liu-West when the effective sample size is low.
Repeat until the posterior variance is below a threshold.

specification.measurement: Single-qubit projective measurement of qubit q in the Z basis, or in the X basis via H before measurement; Qiskit little-endian ordering, so measure(i,i) maps bit i to the last-character position.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Particle-filter Bayesian inference: reweighting, effective-sample-size check, Liu-West resampling, posterior mean and variance, stopping test. Control design on the learned theta is out of scope.
assumptions: Experiment scope chosen by me: 1D open chain, n<=8, product initial state |+>^n
Trotter angles: RZZ(2 J dt) and RX(2 h dt), with Qiskit sign conventions to be checked
The form of v(sigma) is unspecified
Hidden parameters of the target device are simulated by the runner, not by an opaque gate
